title: Procedure call with a bounded execution
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let its execution limits be given, and let $d,p,x,T,T'$ be natural numbers, $l$ and $\mathrm{vals}$ finite lists of integers, and $\mu$ a memory function from natural numbers to integers. Suppose procedure $p$ has a body that, when started at depth $d+1$ with local frame initialized from $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory $\mu$, has an execution of cost at most $T'$ whose final value and memory satisfy $R(r,\mu')$. Assume every pair $(r,\mu')$ satisfying $R$ makes the state with memory $\mu'$ and local frame obtained by setting position $x$ of $l$ to $r$ satisfy $Q$. If each expression in the call's argument list is safe in the state with local frame initialized from $l$ and memory $\mu$, and those expressions evaluate to $\mathrm{vals}$; if $d$ is less than the depth limit; and if the sum of the argument expression costs plus $2+T'$ is at most $T$, then the call to procedure $p$ with those arguments, storing its returned value at position $x$, has an execution of cost at most $T$ from that state to a state satisfying $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: There is a body for procedure p in P that executes at depth d+1 from the frame initialized from vals and memory μ, with cost at most T', and final value and memory satisfying R
Every pair (r, μ') satisfying R gives Q for the state whose memory is μ' and whose local frame is l with position x set to r
Every call argument is safe in the state with frame initialized from l and memory μ
The call arguments evaluate to vals in that state
d is less than the depth limit
The sum of the argument expression costs plus 2+T' is at most T
